8 22 58] Mahabharata [The Section on the Slaying of Karna]
C 8 1318 B 8 31 68 K 8 22 72

"I shall certainly conquer all the <term>Pandavas</term> <gloss>the five sons of King Pandu</gloss> who have gathered today." [58]

Duryodhana said:
"I will do all of this exactly as you intend, Karṇa. Chariots equipped with quivers will follow you directly, O <term>Sutaja</term> <gloss>son of a charioteer, referring to Karṇa's upbringing</gloss>." [59]
"Let carts carry your iron arrows and your arrows feathered with vulture plumes."

<column-break/>

"We and all the other kings will follow you, Karṇa." [60]

Sañjaya said:
"O great king <note>addressing Dhritarashtra</note>, having spoken in this way, your powerful son the king <note>Duryodhana</note> approached the <term>Madraraja</term> <gloss>the King of Madra, Shalya</gloss> and spoke these words:" [61]

->Thus ends the twenty-second chapter of the Karṇa Book in the glorious Mahābhārata.<-

## 23

Sañjaya said:
"Your son, O great king, spoke these words to the King of Madra..."

<column-break/>

"...approaching him with humility, he spoke this sentence out of affection:" [1]
"O you of true vows, O illustrious one, O you who increase the sorrow of your enemies!"

<note>The remainder of the page consists of the critical apparatus, which lists textual variants and manuscript notations for the preceding verses.</note>

<summary>Duryodhana agrees to Karṇa's battle preparations and ensures that supply carts with arrows follow the chariots. Duryodhana then humbly approaches Shalya, the King of Madra, to ask for his assistance.</summary>
